headline: TSMC, the world's largest contract chip maker, reported third-quarter profit of $23.86 billion, beating forecasts as demand for AI chips stayed strong.
score_reason: Facts match the headline; the AI-demand and sixth-record-quarter points come from Reuters and CNBC headlines, the numbers from the Associated Press.
importance_line: Investors in AI hardware and the companies that buy TSMC's chips, such as Nvidia and Apple, read it as a measure of demand for AI chips, though one strong quarter does not show how long that demand will last.
summary: The Associated Press reports that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. earned $23.86 billion, or $4.60 a share, in the third quarter on revenue of $46.72 billion, above analyst estimates of $4.45 a share and $45.62 billion. Reuters and CNBC describe it as a sixth straight quarter of record profit driven by the AI boom.
notes: investing.com original returned HTTP 403, CNBC and Reuters pages blocked. Numbers read from the AP earnings snapshot on Yahoo Finance (automated, Zacks data). 'Sixth straight record' and 'AI boom' are taken from the Reuters and CNBC headlines in Google News, not from article text. Customers Nvidia and Apple per an investingLive preview.
